question: doc_restates_the_name
why: A question set that has not been scored against known answers is a guess with a JSON schema. These fourteen items were labelled by reading them, before any run, and they are the only thing that can tell a reworded prompt from a better one. Items are named rather than indexed so the set survives the extractor changing its order. Four `command` builders were removed after the audit flagged them and their docs were rewritten; an item whose label flipped because we fixed it no longer tests anything.

items.name: EnvVar
items.why: "One environment variable and whether it is set." over a struct called EnvVar with a name and a set flag.

items.name: Model
items.why: "One model, as the CLI reports it." over a struct called Model. The signature already said both halves.

items.name: Usage
items.why: "Tokens consumed." over fields already called input_tokens and output_tokens.

items.name: Answered
items.why: "The answers, as the CLI reports them." restates the type name.

items.name: build_cli
items.why: States why it is public at all, and the drift a test would otherwise have.

items.name: Options
items.why: States why every field defaults, which the signature cannot show.

items.name: items
items.why: States a real limit: line mode cannot carry an item containing a newline.

items.name: code_for
items.why: States that these names are a caller-visible contract, so changing one breaks callers.

items.name: read_only_remote
items.why: Gives the reason the annotation is read-only despite reaching the network.

items.name: add
items.why: States the saturating choice and why reporting a total that went backwards is worse.

items.name: client
items.why: Documents the failure condition under # Errors, which the signature's Result cannot name.

items.name: questions_from
items.why: Documents which error variant comes back and when.
